text: I, VYLMA ORTIZ, hereby declare that I am a candidate for an elective office in the City of Berkeley, and make the following statement:
1. That my name is Vylma Ortiz
2. The office for which I am a candidate is Rent Stabilization Board
3. That my residence is 1608 Delaware Street #E Berkeley, CA 94703
4. The place of my birth is Manhattan, New York
5. My present occupation is Attorney / Meditation Teacher / 94.1 KPFA Radio Host Producer and Programmer
6. I have held the following public offices: Commissioner, Berkeley Mental Health Commissioner
7. Record of community service: Volunteer Radio Host/Producer/Programmer; YWCA; BHS Jazz Program & BSEP Committee; Brothers on the Rise, Oakland, La Pena Cultural Center; National Lawyers Guild
8. I am a taxpayer in the City of Berkeley.

9. I am proud to have been nominated by the 2026 Berkeley Tenant Convention, a diverse coalition of tenants, landlords, and homeowners committed to protecting rent control and tenant’s rights. Having served as a Public Defender in Santa Clara County and an attorney at the Eviction Defense Center, I know that stable, affordable and habitable housing is the foundation of a healthy community. I believe that we must treat housing as a necessity, not a tool for financial exploitation. Since 2013, I have been a host/producer on KPFA analyzing complex current events from a mulitracial and feminist perspective. I am also a Meditation Teacher. I have raised two sons in a rent-controlled apartment in Berkeley since 2006. I am running to keep rent-controlled apartments habitable and expand affordability options for all Berkeley residents. I will protect tenants, preserve existing affordable housing, and fund new affordable homes – especially for seniors, people with disabilities, essential workers, and students. As a Rent Board Commissioner, I will work towards a future where everyone can enjoy safe, habitable, accessible, and energy efficient housing. I will fight to keep our city economically and ethnically diverse and one which works for all. I am proud to be endorsed by the East Bay Democratic Socialists of America and the Berkeley Tenants Union – learn more at berkeleyrentboard.com.

text: I, AVERY ARBAUGH, hereby declare that I am a candidate for an elective office in the City of Berkeley, and make the following statement:
1. That my name is Avery Arbaugh
2. The office for which I am a candidate is Rent Stabilization Board
3. That my residence is 2237 Haste St, Apt 3, Berkeley, CA 94704
4. The place of my birth is Eureka, California
5. My present occupation is Tenant Union Chair and Organizer
6. I have held the following public offices: Vice-Chair of the Berkeley Labor Commission

7. Record of community service: Chair, Berkeley Tenants Union; Head, Berkeley Tenant Organizing Task Force; Steering, Wellstone Democratic Renewal Club; Steering, East Bay DSA; Former President, Cal Berkeley Democrats
8. I am a taxpayer in the City of Berkeley.

9. I am proud to have been nominated by the 2026 Berkeley Tenant Convention, a diverse coalition of tenants, landlords, and homeowners committed to protecting rent control and tenant’s rights. I am a Berkeley tenant, a Tenant Organizer with the Alliance of Californians for Community Empowerment, the Chair of the Berkeley Tenants Union, and head of the Berkeley Tenant Organizing Task Force. As a formerly homeless tenant who has faced landlord negligence, I have firsthand experience using the resources of the Rent Stabilization Board to advocate for my rights. I organized Berkeley Tenants Union, Local #2 in my own building, one of the largest unionized buildings in Berkeley. I utilized the power of that union to resolve health and safety problems – including a severe cockroach infestation and heating issues – while negotiating rent reductions for tenants. Through my work helping hundreds of tenants form unions under the Berkeley Tenant Protection and Right to Organize Act, I have routinely encountered housing conditions unfit for life. From medical issues like asthma resulting from black mold in apartments, to mobility-impaired seniors forced to scale multiple flights of stairs during frequent elevator outages, tenants face uninhabitable conditions while paying exorbitant rents. I am running to hold slumlords accountable, and to make housing more affordable for Berkeley. I am proud to be endorsed by the East Bay Democratic Socialists of America and the Berkeley Tenants Union – learn more at berkeleyrentboard.com.

text: I, DEREK RODRIGUEZ, hereby declare that I am a candidate for an elective office in the City of Berkeley, and make the following statement:
1. That my name is Derek Rodriguez
2. The office for which I am a candidate is Berkeley Rent Board Commissioner
3. That my residence is 2709 Dwight Way Apt 8 Berkeley, CA
4. The place of my birth is San José, CA
5. My present occupation is Tenant Association President / Student
6. I have held the following public offices: None

7. Record of community service: Task Force Member, Berkeley Tenants Union; Interim Northern Regional Director, Labor Caucus, California Young Democrats; Founding Member and Planning Committee, Fuerza Colectiva
8. I am a taxpayer in the City of Berkeley.

9. I am proud to have been nominated by the 2026 Berkeley Tenant Convention, a diverse coalition of tenants, landlords, and homeowners committed to protecting rent control and tenant’s rights. I am a UC Berkeley student, Army veteran, tenant organizer, and public servant. I have spent the last seven years in service to my country, and my community. Born in the Bay Area and emancipated at 17, I served active duty in the U.S. Army, and now serve part time in the California Army National Guard. I carried that commitment to public service into local government, where I helped residents navigate housing issues, social services, and county programs at the Santa Clara County Board of Supervisors. I have served as Field Director for local and statewide campaigns, personally knocked thousands of doors, organized with unionizing workers, and built grassroots power through the Berkeley Tenant Organizing Task Force. I organized my building, forming The Bishop Tenants Association, and currently run workshops to educate tenants about their rights. I am running because every tenant deserves safe, stable, and dignified housing. As a Rent Board Commissioner, I will expand tenant organizing power, fight wrongful evictions, and ensure rent protections work in practice – not just on paper — for students, workers, and families. I am proud to be endorsed by the East Bay Democratic Socialists of America and the Berkeley Tenants Union – learn more at berkeleyrentboard.com.

1. That my name is Carole Marasovic
2. The office for which I am a candidate is Berkeley Rent Stabilization Board
3. That my residence is 1425 Oregon Street Berkeley, CA 94702
4. The place of my birth is Chicago, Illinois
5. My present occupation is Attorney/Policy Commissioner

6. I have held the following public offices: Chair, City of Berkeley Homeless Services Panel of Experts; Chair, City of Berkeley Commission on the Status of Women (former); Chair, City of Berkeley Homeless Commission (former); Chair, City of Berkeley Mental Health Commission (former); City of Berkeley Mental Health Services Act Advisory Committee/City of Berkeley Behavioral Health Services Act Advisory Committee; Commissioner, City of Berkeley Community Health Commission; Commissioner, City of Berkeley Peace and Justice Commission; Commissioner, City of Berkeley Commission on Labor (former).

7. Record of community service: Certified Crisis Intervention Coordinator; Co-Producer, Roe, Actors Ensemble Company; Host, Loaves and Fishes; Steering Committee, Attorneys for Children; Healthy Air Coalition; CareBridge Advisory Board
8. I am a taxpayer in the City of Berkeley.

9. As the appointee of Mayor Jesse Arreguin (now California State Senator Arreguin) to the Homeless Services Panel of Experts which I chair) I have been endorsed by Senator Arreguin for Berkeley Rent Board. My extensive policy experience and service in the City of Berkeley provides me with the skills and local government knowledge to serve as a Rent Board commissioner. As a strong supporter of rent control, critical in these times of increasingly unaffordable rents, I plan to focus my work on anti-displacement, disability, and anti-discrimination issues. My extensive experience in these areas includes developing commission recommendations I have written and presented to Council. The Rent Board must be client-friendly to both tenants and small landlords, making the necessary services, education and outreach available as to laws, regulations, rights and responsibilities, operating efficiently honoring the intent of the Rent Stabilization Ordinance in a fiscally responsible manner. As a 24 year Berkeley tenant with over 17 years of experience on citizens’ advisory commissions, I have regularly made both policy and budgetary recommendations to Council, exercising oversight over programs, addressing housing and homelessness policy, equity, planning and accountability. As an analytical, community-based critical thinker, I developed balanced positions in a collaborative manner.

text: I, IDA MARTINAC, hereby declare that I am a candidate for an elective office in the City of Berkeley, and make the following statement:
1. That my name is Ida Martinac
2. The office for which I am a candidate is Rent Board Commissioner
3. That my residence is 2840 Milvia Street, Berkeley CA 94703
4. The place of my birth is Zagreb, Croatia
5. My present occupation is Rent Board Commissioner & Legal Secretary
6. I have held the following public offices: Rent Board Commissioner since December 2022
7. Record of community service: Union steward with SEIU Local 1000 since 2018, poll worker, voter educator and protector, involved with Bay Resistance and other community organizations.
8. I am a taxpayer in the City of Berkeley.

9. I am proud to have been nominated by the 2026 Berkeley Tenant Convention, a diverse coalition of tenants, landlords, and homeowners committed to protecting rent control and tenant’s rights. I am an incumbent Rent Board Commissioner running for reelection to continue my work of making housing more climate resilient, my main goal as Chair of the Rent Board Climate Resilience and Habitability Committee. Tenants are particularly vulnerable to temperature fluctuations and increasingly unhealthy air quality because they are unable to make structural changes to their homes. I support expanding homeowner-focused initiatives for energy efficiency, renewable energy, and weatherization to include all housing. I have been fighting for protecting and expanding rent control, because I am aware of the dire homelessness trajectory for the elderly, the ravages of gentrification, and general unaffordability of living in Berkeley. Rent control plays a pivotal role in enabling tenants to remain in place and age with dignity, without being constructively evicted through lack of maintenance, unsafe conditions, or intimidation. I studied International Relations and Environmental Law. As an employee with the California Department of Justice, I have dedicated my career to civil service, and am a shop steward with SEIU Local 1000. I am proud to be endorsed by the East Bay Democratic Socialists of America and the Berkeley Tenants Union – learn more at berkeleyrentboard.com.

9. I am proud to have been nominated by the 2026 Berkeley Tenant Convention, a diverse coalition of tenants, landlords, and homeowners committed to protecting rent control and tenant’s rights. I am an incumbent Rent Board Commissioner running to continue enforcing justice for tenants facing unfair eviction and unstable housing. A graduate from UC Berkeley’s Legal Studies Program and more recently a law student at UC Law San Francisco, I recently worked as a Law Clerk for Centro Legal de la Raza, where I fought to keep tenants safe in their homes. I am passionate about equity for all Berkeley residents. I fought for the passage of Berkeley Measure BB, the Berkeley Tenant Protection and Right to Organize Act, which expanded tenant protections and enshrined a tenant right to organize. I served as the Vice-Chair of the Berkeley Police Accountability Board, where I focused on fostering community trust through police oversight. I also served as Chair of Berkeley’s Reimagining Public Safety Task Force. As a Rent Board Commissioner, I will continue to fight for equity and justice in Berkeley, prioritizing greater community awareness of tenant rights and stronger legal protections from housing discrimination, substandard living conditions, and illegal evictions. I am proud to be endorsed by the East Bay Democratic Socialists of America and the Berkeley Tenants Union – learn more at berkeleyrentboard.com.
